To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the nucleus accumbense shell, but not the core, is involved in hyperactivity and impulsiveness in rats.

the core and shell subregions of the nucleus accumbs are separately involved in the control of impulsivity and locomotion, with hyperactive rats exhibiting an enhanced sensitivity to D2/2 receptor activation in both subregions.

the D2/2 receptor agonist quipinrole increased premature responding on the 5-choice serial reaction time test in high impulsive rats, and increased locomotor activity only in high impulsive but not in low impulsive rats, when injected into the nucleus accumben core or shell respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neurobiology of impulsivity, which is a core feature of a number of neuropsychiatric disorders, most notably attention-deficit hyperactivitity disorder (ADHD) and substance use disorders.
understanding the neural basis of attention-deficit hyper-activity disorder (ADHD) and how it is regulated by dopamine D2/3 receptors in the nucleus accu-mbans (NAcb).
identifying the neurochemical basis of attentional impulsivity in the 5-CSR TT.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
D2/3 receptors in the shell sub-region of the nucleus accubens are involved in the regulation of hyperactivity and D2/3 in the core sub-region of the accumbens are involved in impulsivity.
the core and shell sub-region of the NAcb have divergent effects on impulsive responding and locomotor activity.
the core of the accumbens is involved in impulsivity and the shell is involved in locomotor hyperactivity, and these two symptoms of ADHD may not be linked to the same neurochemical system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
D2/3 receptors are hyper-responsive in the NAcb of HI rats.
the NAcb core mediates the impulsivity component and the NAcb shell mediates the hyperactivity component of impulsivity.
D2/3 receptors are involved in impulsivity and locomotion, and these behaviours are regulated by different sub-regions of NAcb in high impulsive rats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nucleus accumben (NAcb) core and shell are involved in impulsivity and locomotion, respectively.
D2/3 receptors in the core and shell subregions of the NAcb have different roles in mediating impulsivity and hyperlocomotion in the rat.
hyperactivity and impulsiveness are regulated by different sub-regions in the nucleus accumbs.
